title: The Western Ghats: A Nature Traveller's Guide
seoTitle: The Western Ghats: A Nature Traveller's Guide | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: A nature traveller's guide to the Western Ghats: UNESCO forests, shola grasslands, waterfalls, the Kaas plateau, and the best places state by state.
description: A guide to the Western Ghats for nature travellers: the range and its UNESCO World Heritage status, shola grasslands, rainforests and waterfalls, the Kaas plateau, and the best places to experience them state by state (Maharashtra's Sahyadri, Goa's Mollem, Karnataka's Agumbe, Kudremukh and Coorg, Kerala's Silent Valley, Wayanad and Munnar, and Tamil Nadu's Nilgiris and Anamalais), with the monsoon and the best seasons.
dek: The Western Ghats run the length of India's west coast, a chain of forests, grasslands and waterfalls recognised by UNESCO for its biodiversity.

hero.alt: Shola grasslands and forest in Kudremukh National Park, Karnataka

intro: The Western Ghats, also called the Sahyadri, run for about 1,600 km parallel to India's west coast, from near the Gujarat-Maharashtra border to the southern tip of the peninsula. They catch the south-west monsoon, which feeds rainforests, waterfalls and the rivers that flow east across the Deccan, including the Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri.

UNESCO inscribed the Western Ghats as a World Heritage Site in 2012, as a group of protected areas across Maharashtra, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu, recognising their exceptional biodiversity. Together with Sri Lanka, they form one of the world's biodiversity hotspots.
quickAnswer: The Western Ghats are a mountain range along India's west coast, inscribed by UNESCO in 2012 for their biodiversity. The best places to experience their nature are the Kaas plateau and Sahyadri forts in Maharashtra, Mollem and Dudhsagar in Goa, Agumbe, Kudremukh and Coorg in Karnataka, Silent Valley, Wayanad and Munnar's Eravikulam in Kerala, and the Nilgiris and Anamalais in Tamil Nadu. The monsoon brings waterfalls; October to March is best for walks.
takeaways: The Western Ghats are a UNESCO World Heritage Site (2012) and a global biodiversity hotspot with Sri Lanka.
The monsoon (June to September) brings waterfalls and blooms; October to March is best for walking.
Shola forest and grassland mosaics are a distinctive landscape of the higher Ghats.
Anamudi, in Eravikulam National Park, is the highest peak in South India.
Many forests are protected; walks are usually guided and permit-based.

items.name: Rainforest
body: Wet evergreen forest at Silent Valley, Agumbe and parts of Wayanad and the Anamalais.

items.name: Shola and grassland
body: Stunted montane forest in valley folds, surrounded by rolling grassland, at Eravikulam, Kudremukh and the upper Nilgiris.

items.name: Laterite plateaus
body: Flat-topped plateaus such as Kaas, which bloom with wildflowers after the monsoon.

items.name: Kaas, Amboli and Mollem
body: The Kaas plateau's flower season, Amboli's rain-soaked forests, and Goa's Mollem forests around Dudhsagar.

items.name: Agumbe, Kudremukh and Coorg
body: Rainforest at Agumbe, grassland treks at Kudremukh, coffee and forest in Coorg and Chikmagalur, and Jog Falls on the Sharavathi.

items.name: Silent Valley, Eravikulam and the Nilgiris
body: Silent Valley's rainforest, the Nilgiri tahr at Eravikulam, Wayanad's forests, and the Nilgiri and Anamalai hills.

sections.heading: The Ghats in the monsoon
paras: From June to September the Ghats are at their greenest, with waterfalls on every slope and clouds in the valleys. It is a wonderful time for drives and short walks, but leeches, closed trails and landslides on ghat roads are part of the deal. September and October often combine full waterfalls with easier access.

sections.heading: Wildlife and birds
paras: The Ghats are home to lion-tailed macaques, Nilgiri tahr, Malabar giant squirrels, great hornbills and many endemic frogs, lizards and birds. Nagarhole, Bandipur, Periyar and Mudumalai are the best-known reserves; sightings are never guaranteed.

sections.heading: Good routes
list: Pune or Mumbai to Kaas, Mahabaleshwar and the Sahyadri forts.
Goa to Mollem, Dudhsagar and Dandeli.
Bengaluru to Coorg, Chikmagalur, Kudremukh and Agumbe.
Kochi to Munnar, Thekkady and Athirappilly.
Coimbatore to the Nilgiris and Valparai.

sections.heading: Travelling lightly
paras: The Ghats are densely settled as well as biodiverse, and many forest roads pass through protected areas. Drive slowly, do not stop or feed animals on forest roads, avoid plastic, and choose local homestays and guides. Night driving is restricted on some forest highways.

safety: Stay on marked trails and viewpoints, and heed local closures after heavy rain.
Permits, entry rules and seasonal closures change; check official sources before you go.
Carry your waste back, avoid loud music, and never feed wildlife.
Leeches are common in the monsoon; wear leech socks and check your legs after walks.
packing: Rain jacket and leech socks in the monsoon

faqs.a: A mountain range running about 1,600 km along India's west coast, known for its forests, waterfalls and biodiversity.

faqs.q: Are the Western Ghats a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
faqs.a: Yes, inscribed in 2012 as a series of protected areas in Maharashtra, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

faqs.q: What is the highest peak in the Western Ghats?
faqs.a: Anamudi, in Kerala's Eravikulam National Park.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit the Western Ghats?
faqs.a: The monsoon for waterfalls and greenery; October to March for walks and treks.

faqs.q: Which states do the Western Ghats cover?
faqs.a: Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
